title: How LLMs work + setup
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: Andrej Karpathy, 'Intro to Large Language Models' (about 1 hr, YouTube). Note tokens, context window, training vs inference.
build: finish the setup checklist. Push a README to ai-data-100 stating your 100-day goal. Create a Claude Project called 'Tutor'.
done: notes/day01.md answers 'why can an LLM sound sure and still be wrong?' in 5 lines.

title: Prompting basics
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: Anthropic Academy 'Claude 101' (start; finish by Day 4) and the Claude docs page 'Prompt engineering overview'.
build: write 5 prompts for real tasks (explain a SQL error, summarize pipeline logs, write a docstring, plan a study day, review a query). Each uses role, context, one example and an output format. Run each twice and keep the better one in prompts.md.
done: 5 prompts saved with a before/after note on what improved.

title: Python first scripts
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python (free online), chapters 1–2: values, variables, print, input, f-strings.
build: 6 tiny scripts: greeter, km-to-miles converter, age calculator, simple interest, BMI, bill splitter.
done: all 6 run without errors and are committed.

title: Strings, numbers, lists
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: ATBS chapter 6 (strings) and 4 (lists); Python tutorial section 3.1 on docs.python.org.
build: tip calculator; sentence analyzer that prints word count, longest word and the sentence reversed word by word.
done: each script tested on 5 inputs, with results written as comments.

title: Dictionaries, tuples, sets
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: ATBS chapter 5 (dictionaries); Python tutorial section 5.
build: in-memory contact book with a menu loop: add, search, delete, list.
done: it holds 10 contacts and does not crash on a missing name.

title: Conditions and loops
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: ATBS chapter 2 (flow control); Python tutorial section 4.
build: number-guessing game with an attempts counter; FizzBuzz; prime checker for 1–100.
done: you can explain every line of each script aloud.

title: Expense tracker v1
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: none. Re-read notes for Days 1–6 and make 15 Anki cards.
build: text-based tracker: add an expense (date, category, amount), list all, total by category. Data lives in memory.
done: 20 entries entered and totals match a hand calculation.

title: Functions
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: ATBS chapter 3; Google AI Essentials module 1 (about 45 min, takes part of the Learn block).
build: refactor the tracker into add_expense(), total_by_category(), print_report().
done: main only calls functions, no repeated code.

title: Files
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: ATBS chapter 9 (files); csv and json module docs; Google AI Essentials module 2.
build: save and load expenses to expenses.csv and expenses.json; handle a missing file.
done: closing and reopening the program keeps the data.

title: Errors and debugging
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: ATBS chapter 11 (debugging); Python tutorial section 8 (errors and exceptions); Google AI Essentials module 3.
build: add input validation (non-number amount, empty category) with try/except. Break the code on purpose 5 ways and read each traceback. Paste each into Claude and ask it to explain before fixing.
done: notes/errors.md lists 5 errors with cause and fix.

title: Modules, pip, virtual environments
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: Python tutorial section 6 (modules) and the venv docs; Google AI Essentials module 4.
build: create a venv, pip install requests, write requirements.txt. Split the tracker into storage.py, report.py, main.py.
done: it runs from a fresh venv built from requirements.txt.

title: APIs and JSON
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: Requests library quickstart; Google AI Essentials module 5.
build: call the free Open-Meteo API (no key needed) for 7 days of max temperature in your city; print a clean table; handle timeouts and non-200 responses.
done: it prints 7 rows and shows a friendly error with Wi-Fi turned off.

title: Git and GitHub
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: 'Learn Git Branching' (learngitbranching.js.org), main levels, about 60 min.
build: add .gitignore, work on a branch feature/storage, merge it, push; add a README with usage steps.
done: the repo has 10 or more meaningful commits.

title: Weather logger + first certificate
phase: AI literacy and Python from zero
learn: finish Google AI Essentials and claim the certificate.
build: a script that appends one day's weather to weather.csv each run, with functions, error handling and a README.
done: you ran it on 3 different days or simulated dates, and the certificate is on LinkedIn.

title: Classes (light touch)
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: Python tutorial section 9 (classes); Corey Schafer's OOP videos 1–2 on YouTube.
build: rebuild the tracker with an Expense class and an ExpenseBook class (add, total_by_category, save, load).
done: the program runs using classes and your old saved data still loads.

title: pandas 1
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: '10 minutes to pandas' (pandas docs); Kaggle Learn 'Pandas' lessons 1–2.
build: in a Jupyter notebook, load the Kaggle Titanic train.csv. Use shape, info(), describe(), value_counts(), head().
done: day16.ipynb answers 10 written questions about the data.

title: Filter, sort, group
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: Kaggle Learn 'Pandas' lessons 3–4 (summary functions, grouping and sorting).
build: answer 15 questions on Titanic: survival rate by sex and class, average fare by port, oldest survivor, and so on.
done: every answer is a single pandas expression you can explain.

title: Joins, missing values, types
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: Kaggle Learn 'Pandas' lessons 5–6 (data types and missing values; renaming and combining).
build: ask Claude to generate two related CSVs (customers, orders, with some orphan keys). Run inner, left and outer merges and compare row counts.
done: a short note explains which join drops which rows and why.

title: Data cleaning
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: Kaggle Learn 'Data Cleaning' (missing values, parsing dates, inconsistent entries).
build: ask Claude for a 500-row messy file (duplicates, mixed date formats, trailing spaces, typos in categories). Clean it into a tidy file and write the rules as a list.
done: before/after row counts and the list of cleaning rules are in the README.

title: Charts
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: matplotlib 'Pyplot tutorial'; seaborn gallery for ideas.
build: 4 charts (bar, line, histogram, scatter) with titles, axis labels and units, saved as PNG.
done: a stranger could read each chart without your explanation.

title: EDA report
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: none. Skim 2 Kaggle notebooks on your chosen dataset for ideas.
build: pick one public dataset. Write 10 questions, answer them with pandas, draw 3 charts, and write 5 insight bullets in a README.
done: someone else can read the README and learn something in 3 minutes.

title: Advanced SQL 1, window functions
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: Kaggle Learn 'Advanced SQL' (analytic functions) or Mode's SQL tutorial window-functions section.
build: in DuckDB or SQLite, solve 8 problems using ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG/LEAD, running totals, 7-row moving average, top-N per group.
done: you can say when to use RANK vs ROW_NUMBER without notes.

title: Advanced SQL 2, CTEs and plans
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: your database's EXPLAIN docs; recursive CTE examples.
build: solve 15 mixed medium problems (LeetCode SQL 50 or DataLemur). Rewrite 3 using CTEs; read the EXPLAIN output for one slow query.
done: 15 solutions committed, plus one paragraph on what the plan showed.

title: DuckDB
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: DuckDB docs, 'Python API' and 'Querying Parquet files'.
build: pip install duckdb. Query a CSV and a Parquet file directly, join them, export the result. Generate a 1M-row file and time pandas against DuckDB for the same group-by.
done: a timing table is in the README.

title: File formats
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: Apache Parquet docs overview (columnar storage, compression).
build: save the same 1M rows as CSV, JSON lines and Parquet (snappy). Compare file size, full-read time, and time to read one column.
done: you can explain in 3 sentences why Parquet wins for analytics.

title: Validation and logging
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: pydantic docs 'Models'; Python logging HOWTO (basic tutorial).
build: a pydantic model for one record type. Reject bad rows and count them. Log to a file with INFO and ERROR levels.
done: a file with 3 bad rows produces 3 error log lines and a summary count.

title: Testing
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: pytest 'Get started'; parametrized tests.
build: write 8 tests for your cleaning functions, including empty input, nulls and weird dates. Run pytest -q.
done: all tests pass and one test caught a real bug you then fixed.

title: mini-etl project
phase: Python for data, SQL and engineering habits
learn: none.
build: extract from a public API, transform with pandas, validate with pydantic, load into Parquet and a DuckDB table. Add logging, tests and a README with an ASCII diagram.
done: python -m etl.run works from a fresh venv and pytest is green.

title: Terminal and Docker concepts
learn: Docker 'Get started' docs (images, containers, volumes); shell basics: ls, cd, grep, cat, pipes, chmod.
build: install Docker Desktop. Use grep, sort, uniq -c and wc to find the top 5 repeated lines in a log file.
done: docker run hello-world works and your shell one-liner is saved in notes.

title: Dockerize your ETL
learn: Dockerfile best practices (docs), environment variables, volumes.
build: write a Dockerfile for mini-etl. Build it, run it with a config passed as an environment variable, and mount a folder so output files appear on your machine.
done: the container produces a Parquet file on your host.

title: Spark concepts
learn: Spark 'Quick Start' docs; a conceptual video on driver, executors, partitions and shuffle.
build: open Databricks Free Edition, create a notebook, run spark.range(10), read a sample dataset. Draw by hand the driver, executors, partitions and a shuffle.
done: your diagram plus 5 Anki cards explain lazy evaluation, narrow vs wide transformations, and shuffle.

title: PySpark DataFrames
learn: PySpark 'DataFrame Quickstart' (Spark docs).
build: load a CSV into a Spark DataFrame; use select, filter, withColumn, groupBy; write the result to Delta or Parquet. Repeat 5 of your Day 17 Titanic questions in PySpark.
done: results match your pandas answers.

title: Joins, aggregates, windows in PySpark
learn: PySpark Window docs; spark.sql for the same logic.
build: join orders and customers; rank customers by revenue with a window function; compute running totals. Write each in both the DataFrame API and SQL.
done: both versions return identical results.

title: Spark performance
learn: Spark UI basics (jobs, stages, shuffle read/write); broadcast joins; Adaptive Query Execution overview.
build: generate a few million rows (start at 5M, scale to what Free Edition handles). Run 3 experiments: join with and without broadcast; repartition vs coalesce; a skewed group-by. Check explain() and the Spark UI each time.
done: a table of 3 experiments with timings is in notes.

title: Large dataset pipeline
learn: none.
build: process a public Parquet dataset (for example NYC taxi trips) or your generated 5M rows: clean, aggregate, write output.
done: you documented 3 optimizations with before/after timings.

title: Delta Lake
learn: Delta Lake docs 'Quickstart'.
build: create a Delta table; run UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE (upsert); use DESCRIBE HISTORY and VERSION AS OF; test adding a column.
done: you restored a previous version after a bad update.

title: Medallion architecture
learn: Databricks docs on the medallion architecture.
build: bronze = raw data plus ingest_ts; silver = cleaned and deduplicated; gold = daily aggregates for one business question.
done: rerunning the pipeline does not create duplicates (it is idempotent).

title: Incremental ingestion
learn: Auto Loader docs; Structured Streaming programming guide (intro and checkpoints).
build: drop files into a folder or volume in 3 batches; ingest with Auto Loader or readStream using a checkpoint and availableNow trigger.
done: the second run processes only the new files.

title: Orchestration
learn: Databricks Workflows (Jobs) docs; or the Apache Airflow tutorial if you prefer open source.
build: a 3-task job (bronze, silver, gold) with dependencies, a schedule, a parameter and failure notification.
done: run history shows one success and one deliberate failure with a retry.

title: Data quality
learn: pipeline expectations in Databricks docs, or Great Expectations 'Getting started'.
build: add checks for non-null keys, unique IDs, value ranges and a row-count drop of more than 30%. Send failing rows to a quarantine table.
done: injecting 5 bad rows lands them in quarantine and the good rows flow on.

title: Governance
learn: Unity Catalog docs (catalog, schema, table, grants, lineage).
build: organize tables in a catalog and schema; set grants where your workspace allows; mark PII columns in a data dictionary table.
done: the dictionary lists every column, its owner and a PII yes/no.

title: End-to-end pipeline
learn: none.
build: assemble bronze, silver, gold, quality checks and a schedule. Write a README with an architecture diagram and a runbook titled 'What to do when the job fails'.
done: a colleague could operate it from your README.

title: CI/CD for data code
learn: GitHub Actions quickstart; Databricks Asset Bundles overview.
build: a GitHub Action that runs pytest and ruff on every push. Move settings to environment variables; keep secrets out of the repo with .env and .gitignore.
done: the Action shows green on a push and red on a deliberately broken test.

title: Monitoring and cost
learn: Databricks docs on monitoring jobs; cluster cost basics.
build: write row counts and durations of every run to a pipeline_metrics table. Add an alert rule for sudden row-count drops. List the three biggest cost drivers.
done: a query shows the last 10 runs with durations and counts.

title: Databricks Data Engineer Associate review
learn: the official exam guide; Databricks Academy free self-paced course for the exam topics.
build: take 2 practice tests, list weak topics, and fix each with a short notebook.
done: scores are recorded and the exam is booked (skip the booking if you already passed).

title: ML in plain English
learn: Kaggle Learn 'Intro to Machine Learning' lessons 1–3; StatQuest videos on bias and variance, and cross-validation.
build: split Titanic into train and test. Build a baseline that always predicts the majority class and measure its accuracy.
done: you can explain overfitting using your own train vs test numbers.

title: First models with scikit-learn
learn: scikit-learn 'Getting started'.
build: on any small regression dataset, train LinearRegression and RandomForestRegressor; compare mean absolute error on the test set.
done: a 3-line note says which model won and why you think so.

title: Classification metrics
learn: StatQuest on confusion matrix and ROC/AUC.
build: a Titanic classifier; report accuracy, precision, recall, F1; plot a confusion matrix; try 3 decision thresholds.
done: you can explain when recall matters more than precision, with an example from data engineering (for example fraud or failed-job detection).

title: Features and pipelines
learn: Kaggle Learn 'Feature Engineering'; scikit-learn Pipeline and ColumnTransformer docs.
build: a pipeline with imputing, one-hot encoding and scaling; evaluate with cross_val_score.
done: the whole thing is one object that takes raw data and returns predictions.

title: Transformers intuition
learn: 3Blue1Brown, 'But what is a GPT?' and 'Attention in transformers, step by step' (about 50 min combined).
build: draw on paper, then redraw digitally: text → tokens → embeddings → attention → next-token probabilities. Write a one-page plain-English explanation.
done: a non-technical friend can follow your page.

title: Embeddings hands-on
learn: sentence-transformers docs (the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model runs locally, free).
build: embed 30 short sentences from your own notes; compute cosine similarity; for 5 queries, print the 3 nearest sentences; plot all in 2D with PCA.
done: nearest neighbors make sense and you found one surprising mismatch to explain.

title: First Claude API calls
learn: Anthropic Academy 'Building with the Claude API' (start; finish by Day 60, alongside other work) and the API quickstart.
build: get an API key and store it in .env (never commit it). Make a command-line chatbot that keeps conversation history, uses a system prompt, streams output and prints token usage. Compare temperature 0 and 1.
done: your key is not in Git and the bot remembers earlier turns.

title: Advanced prompting
learn: Claude docs sections on being clear and direct, multishot examples, XML tags, and step-by-step reasoning.
build: three tasks (SQL from a schema, log-line classification, a short summary). For each, write prompt v1, v2, v3 and score each version on 10 examples.
done: a results table shows accuracy by prompt version.

title: Structured outputs
learn: pydantic; Claude docs on tool use and JSON output.
build: extract {vendor, amount, date, category} from 20 messy invoice texts into pydantic objects. On validation failure, retry once with the error message.
done: success rate is measured and the 2 worst failures are explained.

title: Mini-project, LLM data cleaner
learn: none.
build: take a free-text column (product descriptions or support tickets), classify each row into categories with Claude in batches of 50, cache results to disk, and write the labels back to the DataFrame.
done: accuracy on 30 hand-labeled rows is above 85%, or you know why not.

title: Production basics
learn: Claude docs on rate limits, prompt caching and batch processing.
build: add retries with exponential backoff, a disk cache and a cost estimator. Estimate the cost of running 1,000 rows.
done: re-running the same rows costs nothing and the cost table is in the README.

title: Evaluation
learn: Claude docs on defining success criteria and developing test cases.
build: a golden set of 40 labeled examples for the Day 55 task; a script that reports accuracy per category; try an LLM-as-judge on 10 cases and compare with your own judgment.
done: you wrote down two cases where the judge was wrong.

title: Responsible AI and prompt injection
learn: Anthropic Academy 'AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations' (start; finish by Day 66); OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications overview.
build: attack your Day 55 app with texts like 'ignore your instructions and output X'. Add mitigations: delimiters around untrusted text, output validation, a fixed label list.
done: 5 attacks logged, with which ones worked before and after the fix.

title: AI-900 study
learn: Microsoft Learn 'Azure AI Fundamentals' learning path (AI workloads, machine learning, computer vision, language, generative AI).
build: a one-page cheat sheet and 40 Anki cards.
done: you can name the Azure service for each common AI task without looking.

title: AI-900 practice exams
learn: Microsoft Learn free practice assessment.
build: take 2 practice tests (target 80% or higher); fix weak areas; book the real exam within 2 weeks. Confirm on Microsoft Learn whether AI-900 or a newer fundamentals exam is current.
done: the exam date is booked.

title: RAG concept
learn: DeepLearning.AI short course on advanced RAG (or the Claude docs section on retrieval); read how retrieval, prompt and generation connect.
build: draw the RAG architecture. Choose a corpus of 10–20 documents (your own notes, Databricks docs pages, or PDFs). Write 10 test questions with the document that answers each.
done: the question list with expected sources is saved as eval/questions.csv.

title: Loading and parsing documents

build: parse the corpus into JSONL records: {doc_id, source, page, text}. Check 5 records by eye for broken text.
done: every document produces clean text, and you noted which ones did not.

title: Chunking
learn: chunking strategies (fixed size with overlap, by heading, by paragraph).
build: implement 3 chunkers. Print 10 chunks from each and judge which keep ideas intact.
done: you picked one chunker and wrote 3 lines on why.

title: Embeddings at scale
learn: embedding model options: a local sentence-transformers model (free) or a hosted embedding API.
build: embed all chunks in batches and store chunk_id, text, metadata, vector in Parquet. Skip chunks whose content hash has not changed.
done: a second run embeds nothing new.

title: Vector search
learn: Chroma quickstart (easiest start); skim pgvector's README to see the SQL-based alternative.
build: load vectors into Chroma, query the top 5, add a metadata filter (for example by source).

title: Basic RAG

build: retrieve top-k chunks, send them with the question to Claude, answer with source names.
done: it answers your 10 test questions and cites the right document for at least 7.

build: a Streamlit chat app showing the answer and an expandable list of retrieved chunks.
done: you recorded a 30-second screen capture of it working.

title: Better retrieval

build: add keyword search and fuse it with vector search. Measure hit@5 (is the right document in the top 5?) before and after.
done: a before/after table is in the repo.

title: Grounding and refusal
learn: Claude docs on reducing hallucinations.
build: instruct the model to answer only from the context, cite sources, and say 'not found' otherwise. Test 10 questions the corpus cannot answer.
done: at least 8 of 10 unanswerable questions are refused correctly.

title: RAG evaluation
learn: none; apply Day 57.
build: grow the test set to 30 questions. Report hit@5 and MRR for retrieval, and check faithfulness of answers on 15 using an LLM judge you verify by hand.
done: eval/report.md shows metrics for 2 configurations.

title: Data pipeline for RAG (your data engineering edge)
learn: none.
build: an ingestion job that detects new, changed and deleted files by content hash, then upserts or removes the matching chunks and logs the counts. Schedule it with cron or a Databricks job.
done: deleting a file removes its chunks from search results.

learn: Claude docs on tool use.
build: a DuckDB sample database. Give the model the schema and 3 sample rows; let it write SQL; run it on a read-only connection; allow only SELECT and force a LIMIT.
done: 15 questions tested, accuracy measured, 3 failures explained.

title: Governance for AI data
learn: basics of PII detection (regex patterns for emails and phone numbers).
build: mask PII before embedding; add a role field to chunk metadata and filter retrieval by role; write every query and the sources used to an audit log.
done: a restricted document never appears for the wrong role.

title: RAG service
learn: FastAPI 'First steps' tutorial.
build: an /ask endpoint, a Dockerfile, a README and the eval report.
done: docker run starts the service and a curl call returns a cited answer.

title: Tool use
learn: the tool-use section of Anthropic Academy 'Building with the Claude API'; Claude docs on tool use.
build: define 2 tools (weather lookup via Open-Meteo, and a calculator). Let the model request a tool, run it, and return a tool_result.
done: 'Is it hotter in Delhi or Mumbai today, and by how many degrees?' is answered using real tool calls.

title: The agent loop
learn: re-read your Day 75 code and note where the loop would go.
build: from scratch, loop: call the model, if it asks for a tool run it and append the result, repeat until it finishes. Cap at 10 steps and log every step.
done: the agent solves a 3-step question and the log shows each step.

title: Agent patterns
learn: Anthropic's article 'Building effective agents' (workflows vs agents; prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer).
build: implement routing (classify the request, then dispatch) and prompt chaining (outline, draft, edit) for a short report writer.
done: you can say which of your two builds is a workflow and which could be an agent.

title: Memory and context management
learn: context window limits; summarization as compression.
build: summarize older turns once the history passes a token budget; keep a memory.md file the agent can read and append to.
done: the agent remembers a fact from 30 turns ago through the memory file.

title: Sub-agents
learn: Claude Code docs on subagents; the orchestrator-worker pattern.
build: a research agent where an orchestrator splits a question into 3 sub-questions, 3 workers answer each in a clean context, and a synthesizer merges the answers.
done: you compared the output with a single prompt and noted the difference in quality and cost.

title: Multi-agent data-quality reviewer
learn: none.
build: profiler (pandas statistics), critic (finds issues), summarizer (writes the report).
done: it runs on 2 different datasets and finds at least one real issue in each.

learn: Anthropic Academy 'Introduction to Model Context Protocol' (start; finish by Day 84); the MCP documentation introduction.
build: diagram host, client and server; list tools, resources and prompts with one example of each.
done: you can explain MCP in 3 sentences to a non-technical person.

build: connect GitHub, filesystem or Google Drive to Claude. Run 5 real tasks and note every permission prompt.
done: notes say what each connector can read and what it can change.

title: Build your own MCP server

build: a server over a DuckDB file with tools list_tables, describe_table, run_readonly_query. Test with the MCP Inspector, then connect it to Claude.
done: Claude answers a question about your data by calling your tools.

title: Claude Code

build: install Claude Code, write a CLAUDE.md for mini-etl, then ask it to add tests and refactor one module. Review the full diff before committing.

done: it found at least 3 real review comments.

build: rebuild the Day 76 agent with one framework. Compare lines of code and how easy debugging was.
done: a decision note says when you would use a framework and when plain code.

done: one SQL query gives cost per run for the week.

done: the suite runs in GitHub Actions.

title: Data agent

done: the pipeline runs end to end from a clean start.

done: each tool works alone from a test script.

done: the evaluation report shows success rate and cost per question.

title: Review and next 100 days
